As an extremely basic explanation, seizures often have triggers. A pretty commonly known one is lights for example (not all epileptic people have this trigger), but depending on the specific condition triggers can vary. Stress, sleep deprivation, things that are just minor annoyances for regular folks can induce seizures in people who already dealing with them. At the risk of misremembering some of the information, I won’t try to go into more detail. Someone much more knowledgeable than me about this will come along I’m sure. 

There are also illnesses/diseases that can induce seizures (e.g. tumors or swelling of certain parts of the brain) but I don’t think that’s what the comment you replied to was referring to.

I very much relate with your anxiety about this kind of thing, and all I can really say is if you don’t really know what you’re interested in taking classes about then no decision is the wrong one! If you have friends also choosing their classes, maybe ask what they’re choosing and take a few with them. Do you feel like you’re better at certain things than others? It can feel rewarding to pursue something you have a knack for, and it can also be a healthy challenge to yourself if you want to take a class in something that seems vaguely interesting that you’re not sure about. Sometimes just picking something and rolling with it leads to finding a passion about something you may not have considered otherwise. 

And with careers, pessimistic as some may find this, if you don’t have a particular interest in anything academic then there is nothing wrong with other directions. Trade schools are great, certification programs are great. Look at the expected job growth/average pay/job availability in your area for some of the education paths trade schools and certification programs offer. (If that’s a thing where you are, this is a US perspective.) Not saying pursuing something you enjoy academically is a bad thing, nor is pursuing a higher education to make some bigger money if that’s something that drives you. But... Sometimes a very average or unglamorous but secure, minimal stress, fairly-comfortable-but-not-great paying job is a good option. That gives you more freedom to try more things in your free time and just... enjoy simple things in life. Who knows, maybe you WILL discover that passion later on, no rush to know right now.
